name: Sanctuary (Zero-G)
description: The first half of the 2003 'Twin Moons' project. Acting as the 'Anchor', this album features exclusively female vocals from Cassidy O'Connell. It is the ultimate showcase of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™—a mathematically precise, zero-gravity atmospheric masterpiece recorded while the band constructed their permanent Blacksburg studio. It represents finding a peaceful, silent sanctuary in the endless black.
subtitle: The 2003 "Twin Moons" Project (Moon 1)
linerNotes: In 2003, the band refused to choose between their two identities. Instead, they released two albums on the same day: a "Twin Moons" concept exploring the two sides of their survival.

Moon 1: Sanctuary (Zero-G) is Cassidy's album. It is a lush, atmospheric, electronic masterwork designed to replicate the sensation of weightlessness. For Ryan, who lives with constant physical gravity and chronic pain from the 1990 crash, this music was built as a sonic sensory-deprivation tank—a place where the body doesn't hurt anymore.

studioArchives.title: The "Tidal Lock" Mix
studioArchives.content: Engineered using binaural 3D audio techniques. The synthesizers are mixed to pan in slow, elliptical orbits around the listener's head, mimicking the physics of the "Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound."

studioArchives.title: The Twin Moons Concept
studioArchives.content: Every track on Moon 1 shares a tempo and key signature with its counterpart on Moon 2: Mile Marker 98. If played simultaneously, the ambient synths of Moon 1 fit perfectly into the sonic gaps of the heavy guitars on Moon 2.
